assessment_scope: Formal independent first-pass Delivery Review of the sole registered primary plan docs/plans/2026-09-17-complete-model-test-coverage.md at its exact inspected identity, under approved Design Review design-review-final and Proposal Review proposal-review. The complete plan was read, all 24 model-owner allocations and section/parent responsibilities were traced to their milestones and proof groups, and timing/reporting, public artifact boundaries, semantic assessment and closeout contracts were checked against their current owners. Current CLI inspection confirmed all 104 upstream Design subjects and the approved proposal remain unchanged, prior material finding is reporter-resolved, and the registered primary plan matches the inspected file. Selected command and generator sources were inspected for feasibility. The Delivery package contains this plan only; supporting Designs, examples, catalogs and implementation sources are governing basis, not additional plan members or newly approved implementation.
independence_basis: Runtime /root authored the primary plan under root-plan-author. Runtime /root/design_review independently read the full final plan and assessed its sequence, requirement-to-proof allocation, recovery and upstream reliance without editing the plan, navigation, Designs or implementation. This runtime previously performed independent Design Review, not Design or plan authorship; its prior approved Design judgment is a separate upstream assessment. No subagent authored or participated in this Delivery Review. Separation is based on actual authorship and runtime work performed, not actor labels or a new turn.
limitations: This approval covers the exact primary plan for subsequently authorized implementation. The current isolated invocation performs Delivery Review only; it does not initialize work, advance workflow, authorize automatic implementation or grant external-action permission.

M1 still must establish the actual complete executable population, current assertion/fixture gaps and measurement limitations. Planning adequacy is not completed inventory, implemented reporting, measured test cost, proof-gap closure or test/fixture alignment.

The reviewer performed read-only engineering/command inspection and no runtime tests, scenario executions, plan edits or implementation changes. Existing plan-authoring-validation evidence is attributable author evidence with its stated structural scope; future proof must record actual results on applicable subjects.

No milestone/final Code Review, successful Verify, branch readiness, PR readiness or release readiness is established. Proposed semantic and conditional operational proof retains the approved Design and plan limitations until actually assessed.
rationale: Authority and scope: the exact registered plan names the current approved Design Review and preserves all four proposal outcomes. All 24 document models, section-owned Implement/Bugfix/CI/Development responsibilities, parent interactions and surviving historically scoped obligations receive allocation. The user-selected Markdown planning boundary is explicit: authored catalog JSON remains unchanged; native discovery supplies executable inventory and generated execution-result JSON is the separately approved product reporting output. A necessary frozen-reference conflict returns to Design before dependent changes.

Traceability: each Requirements covered row links the governing requirement basis to owning architecture, implementation milestone and named proof group. Milestone descriptions supply the observations, fixture/assessment boundary, execution point, commands or manual evidence, and completion conditions. M1/TG-1 reconciles every current group and caller; M3/TG-3 realizes the method; M4/TG-4 covers Authoring; M5/TG-5 Foundations/Discovery/Learning; M6/TG-6 capability/Workflow/Assessment/Handoff; M7/TG-7 CLI/Records/Installation; M8/TG-8 Engineering/Validation/Packaging/Release. TG-FINAL-1/2/3 provide additional complete-population and parent composition proof. This is proportional group-level allocation, not a test-function quota or a list of commands mistaken for coverage.

Safe sequence and intermediate states: M1 establishes source, caller/discovery and actual assertion/fixture scope while preserving suites; M2 extends the existing executor/reporting and closes measurement/reachability gaps before relevant product-suite changes; M3 establishes usable authored/generated guidance before M4 through M6 rely on it. M4 through M6 coordinate shared fixtures and receiving-owner observations; M7 retains public storage/installer proof, and M8 consumes generated and packed-consumer proof before final integration. Milestone completion requires independent review and unsettled required protection blocks affected progress. No actual gap is deferred solely to final Verify.

Timing allocation: TG-2A/B/C and TG-FINAL-3 cover native Python/Node identity, generated/imported/direct-only populations, unique launch attribution, worker-versus-wall intervals, unstarted work, ranking without selection changes, cross-mode compatibility and exact dirty-source measurement basis. Pre-instrumentation observations retain their limitations; the reconciled complete baseline precedes alignment, and scope/boundary changes cannot be called speedup. Manual reviews and unauthorized live operations receive no invented runtime. Additional caller commands are concretized from M1 evidence rather than treating broad-smoke or the listed commands as a complete population.

Report safety and failure proof: M2 allocates invalid option/closed-value precedence, legacy/generic destination agreement, symlink/source/capture collisions, concurrent writers, child-environment isolation, serialization/replacement failure, controlled interruption and partial discovery. Independent deterministic timing fixtures establish arithmetic while small real workers establish lifecycle cost and cleanup. Prior report bytes, unrelated data and existing nonzero exit precedence remain protected; recovery restores the reporting slice and its readers together.

Proof quality and maintenance: the plan requires coherent valid controls, independently expected outcomes and defining negative faults at the observation boundary. Unknown protection blocks removal; retained/replacement proof and caller reachability must be reconciled. M7 requires actual request/persistence/recovery observations, and M8 explicitly retains real archive, packed CLI, installation and controlled provider boundaries, including the identified packed empty-unit and unsafe-destination gaps. Shared-helper changes trigger affected reassessment. Counts, matching production-derived expectations and a cheaper passing stub cannot establish equivalence.

Semantic and operational proof: the manual-proof contract identifies concrete control/fault packets, exact method/resource/input/output subjects, independently expected decisions and prohibited effects, an independent assessor, and durable observed outcomes. M3 through M6 and applicable M8 procedures receive explicit execution allocation. Such artifact assessment has honest limits and cannot be represented as target-agent runtime or live publication/incident evidence. Future-event non-applicability needs a scoped owner/assessor account; currently applicable deterministic and semantic gaps remain required.

Feasibility and validation: the referenced native suite entrypoints and principal implementation paths exist; package.json supplies the named native Node test command, ci.sh supports the existing modes and worker budget, and build-adapters.py supplies the referenced generation/check surface. The new duration/report example is explicitly reserved for post-M2 use. Commands start focused and may rely on an applicable selected execution instead of duplicate direct reruns. The plan does not fabricate an engineering-effort estimate before M1 exposes missing proof, and routes a discovered behavioral decision gap before dependent implementation.

Recovery and authority: each milestone defines its bounded failure risk, restoration path and completion limit. Rollback preserves unrelated work, original source/fixture state, existing failure evidence and required detection; it cannot restore retired compatibility without a governing decision. Private repositories, destinations, candidates and controlled provider outcomes keep tests within the requested authority. No PR, hosted mutation, publication, push or merge is inferred from qualification or review.

Closeout allocation: every implementation milestone hands its complete slice to independent Code Review. The named final whole-change Code Review checkpoint depends on all M1 through M8 work and required corrections and assesses cross-milestone interactions; distinct successful Verify follows it. Integrated proof and milestone reviews cannot substitute for that checkpoint. This satisfies RC-SR-11/12/13 without claiming that saving the plan or this review completes implementation.

Combined judgment: necessary authority, exact upstream basis, primary-plan membership and actual independence are present. Sequencing and proof adequacy were assessed together against the complete required scope; no supported material allocation defect, unsafe sequence or unresolved necessary decision remains. No findings are raised. Author structural/prose/CI evidence is supplemental and does not substitute for this semantic assessment.
summary: The primary Markdown plan provides a coherent and reviewable sequence for complete model test alignment and attributable execution-cost reporting. Its owner-based milestones, negative and integrated proof, baseline safeguards, recovery paths and final review/Verify dependencies adequately operationalize the approved Design while preserving the requested no-JSON-catalog-refinement scope.
